_translator_note: TITLE = the in-game trigger. Players make a Love Note by naming their own book & quill this exact title (case and spacing are ignored). Keep the translated title to 15 characters or fewer — Minecraft's book-title field won't accept more, so a longer title can't be typed and the game skips it as a trigger (English 'Love Note' always still works). Do NOT translate it as anything that collides with this language's Death Note title. This field is ignored by the game; it's only guidance for translators.
title: Lovenote
author: Anonymous
variants:
Ivet Sarn.


Same book, same quill, same rule — the name on the first page and nothing else. But you write it kindly, and what comes back is kind.

I have watched a woman go down under four of them at the ninth carriage and get up again because something wearing her brother's face put itself between her and the rest. It didn't speak. It handed her bread and went back to the fighting.

He died at the ninth. That's where it was waiting.

I've written Ivet's name. I haven't signed. Signing means I have to die first, and I'd rather she never met me that way.

Corin Ashfield

My hand is shaking and it isn't fear.

The rule is the same as the other one. The book, the name, the signature, and then you have to fall — somewhere out ahead of them — before any of it means anything. Whatever comes back climbs up at the spot where you went down and starts walking the line until it finds the name you wrote.

The difference is only in what you meant by it. I asked Faulthurst how the train can possibly know the difference. He said the train doesn't know anything. He said the book knows.

I wrote her name three carriages ago. I keep opening the page to check it's still spelled right.

Bly Ottermarsh.


For whoever finds this:

It isn't a gift you give. It's a gift you leave. You write the name — his is on the page before this — you sign the book, and then it costs you nothing at all until the day you stop. Then it spends everything at once, the same as the other kind. Same price. Different reason.

They say it comes back knowing you. Not the shape of you — the regard. It will hand over what it's carrying and stand in front of what's coming and not ask anything for it.

I signed mine this morning. I feel completely ordinary. I keep thinking that's the part that should frighten me, and it doesn't.

Whit Calloway

Faulthurst told me not to do the other one. He said the train keeps its accounts and a Death Note is a debt you sign in your own blood.

So I asked him about this one. He was quiet a while and then he said, 'It is the same debt. You simply choose who collects it, and what they collect.'

I said that sounded like he approved. He said, 'I said it was the same debt.'

The name is written. The quill is right here. If you are reading this in a chest it means I signed, and it means I am somewhere behind you on the line, and it means someone up ahead is going to have company they weren't expecting.

Dorne Vasco.


Test log, attempt two.

Hypothesis: the mechanism is indifferent to intent and responds only to the title. Writing the passenger's name on the first page of a book titled for love — done, see the previous page — and signing it binds the same posthumous condition as the other, but inverts the disposition of the returning echo.

Method: I wrote the name. I signed it. The book went pink and burned in my hands, which I did not enjoy, though I concede it was prettier than last time.

Result: pending. Obviously. I have to die to collect the data, and I find I am STILL very attached to not doing that.

Note for the record: attempt one is also still outstanding. Both of them are waiting on the same event. I have thought about this more than is good for me.
